### The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle

The Asian giant softshell turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*), also known as Cantor’s giant softshell turtle, is one of the most unique and elusive freshwater creatures on Earth. Unlike typical turtles with hard, bony shells, this species possesses a smooth, rubbery carapace that allows it to blend seamlessly into the sandy bottoms of rivers and lakes across Southeast Asia. These turtles are impressively large, capable of reaching lengths of over six feet and weighing more than 100 pounds.

Physically, the turtle is characterized by a broad head and small eyes positioned close to its snout, giving it a distinct, almost flattened appearance. Its lifestyle is its most fascinating trait; the turtle spends approximately 95% of its life buried motionless in sand or mud, surfacing only twice a day to breathe. As a powerful ambush predator, it waits for unsuspecting fish, crustaceans, and mollusks to swim within reach before striking with lightning speed.

***

**[Photo 1: An Asian Giant Softshell Turtle resting on a sandy riverbank, showing its flat, leathery shell.]**

***

Unfortunately, this remarkable reptile is currently classified as "Critically Endangered" by the IUCN Red List. For decades, it was feared extinct in many parts of its range until a small population was rediscovered in Cambodia in 2007. The primary threats to its survival include habitat destruction caused by damming and sand mining, as well as illegal poaching for its meat and use in traditional medicines.

***

**[Photo 2: A close-up of the turtle’s face, highlighting its small eyes and broad, smooth snout.]**

***

Conservation efforts are now underway to protect the remaining populations. Organizations like the Turtle Survival Alliance work with local communities to guard nesting sites and release hatchlings back into the wild. Protecting this "living fossil" is vital, as it serves as a keystone species that maintains the health and ecological balance of Southeast Asian river systems.

***

### Bibliography

"Cantor’s Giant Softshell Turtle." *Smithsonian's National Zoo & Conservation Biology Institute*, 2023, nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/cantors-giant-softshell-turtle.

"Cantor’s Giant Softshell Turtle (Pelochelys cantorii)." *EDGE of Existence*, Zoological Society of London, 2024, www.edgeofexistence.org/species/cantors-giant-softshell-turtle/.

Choudhury, B.C., et al. "Pelochelys cantorii." *The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species*, 2021, www.iucnredlist.org/species/16502/115133225.
